title: Alpha and Omega (Apocalypse 1:8–18)
hookLine: John on Patmos sees the living one; the letters are cut into the Easter candle

cards: It's the dark of Holy Saturday night. Outside a church a fire crackles, and a priest holds a tall new candle, the paschal candle, which will stand near the altar through Easter.
Following the rite, he may trace a cross into the wax with a stylus: the Greek letter alpha above it, omega below, and the four numbers of the current year, one in each corner.
He presses in five grains of incense for the wounds of Christ, and lights it from the fire. Those letters come from the first chapter of the Apocalypse.

teach.h: A TO Z, AND EVERYTHING BETWEEN.
teach.b: Early in the book, God speaks. In the Douay-Rheims: "I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, saith the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty."
Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, omega the last. In English, A to Z. And A to Z means every letter in between too, every word that could ever be spelled.
Then John says where he is: on the island of Patmos, for the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.

teach.h: A VOICE BEHIND HIM ON PATMOS.
teach.b: On the Lord's day he hears a voice behind him like a trumpet. He turns and sees seven golden candlesticks, and among them one like the Son of man. White hair like wool.
Eyes like a flame. A voice like many waters. A face shining like the sun.

teach.h: HE FALLS; A HAND LAID ON HIM.
teach.b: John falls at his feet like a dead man. And the figure lays his right hand on him. "Fear not. I am the First and the Last."
I was dead, he says, and now I'm alive forever, and I hold the keys of death. Notice the title. In Isaiah, the first and the last is what God calls himself.
Here the risen Christ says it.

teach.h: THE YEAR CARVED ON THE CANDLE.
teach.b: That's why the priest carves those letters into the Easter candle, saying that all time belongs to Christ, and the ages too.
This year goes on the same wax. Whatever happens between its first page and its last, it's inside his A to Z.

how: At the Easter Vigil, the priest marks the new paschal candle with a cross, the letters alpha and omega and the numerals of the year, and may insert five grains of incense; the candle burns at Masses through the Easter season and at baptisms and funerals through the year.

games.q: you're John on Patmos. you turn toward a voice like a trumpet and see a figure with eyes like flame and a face like the sun. you fall at his feet as if dead. what does he do?
o: lays his right hand on you and says, fear not.
disappears before you can look up.
games.why: he laid his right hand on John. fear not. I am the First and the Last, and alive, and was dead.

practice: With a fingertip, on your palm or a table, slowly trace a capital A as you breathe in, then an omega, a horseshoe shape with little feet, as you breathe out.

Then let the space between the two letters hold your day: the beginning, the end, and everything in the middle. If you pray, rest in the line I am the First and the Last; if you don't, just keep tracing and breathing.

wordCard.voice: Patmos, the island. Where John received the vision of the Apocalypse, including Christ's words: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the first and last letters of the alphabet (Apocalypse 1:8), carved on the Easter candle.

carryVoice: Your line: the first and the last. Alpha above, omega below, and this year in between. See you tomorrow.
